title: Attackers Actively Probing for Upgrade-Window RCE Vulnerability in WordPress Core
content_md: On October 28th, 2026, the WordPress Security Team released WordPress 7.1.4 , along with backported security releases for older branches, addressing several security issues, most notably an Unauthenticated Remote Code Execution vulnerability in WordPress core, identified as CVE-2026-119977 . The vulnerability affects WordPress core versions 4.7 through 7.1.3 and can be leveraged by unauthenticated attackers to execute code on the server during a core upgrade, which can lead to complete site compromise. Since this is a race condition vulnerability that can only be exploited during the short window while a core upgrade is in progress, successfully exploiting it to achieve remote code execution is difficult in practice. Our records indicate that attackers started targeting this vulnerability on the same day it was disclosed. The Wordfence Firewall has already blocked over 240,000 exploit attempts targeting this vulnerability. Wordfence Premium , Wordfence Care , and Wordfence Response users received a firewall rule to protect against known exploits targeting this vulnerability in WordPress core on October 28, 2026. Sites using the free version of Wordfence will receive the same protection 30 days later on

CVE-2026-119977.evidence: Attackers actively probing for the upgrade-window RCE; exploit code or confirmed intrusion not reported
